anomalies.observed: UART3_FCC2 pin 3 sits on net NET0014 together with FCC2 pin 48 (VCAP, power_out). UART3_FCC2 pin 4 sits on net NET0101 together with FCC2 pin 73 (VCAP, power_out). The UART3 signal pins are therefore tied to the MCU's internal regulator output pins. The USART3 candidate pins PD8 (FCC2 pin 55) and PD9 (FCC2 pin 56) are not wired to the connector.
anomalies.expected: UART3 connector signal pins should connect to USART3 pins (e.g. PD8/PD9), and an MCU VCAP pin should only connect to its decoupling capacitor, never to an external connector.
anomalies.impact: UART3 would be non-functional, and the VCAP regulator outputs would be loaded and shorted to the external connector. This can disturb the MCU core supply and any device on the connector.

anomalies.observed: NAVC2 VSS pins 18 and 63 form a net named Net-(NAVC2-VSS-Pad18) that contains no ground node. VSSA (pin 12) is unconnected. None of the NAVC2 ground pins appear on the GND net, although the FCC2 VSS pins do.
anomalies.expected: All VSS and VSSA pins of the navigation MCU should be on GND, as the FCC2 VSS pins are.
anomalies.impact: The navigation MCU has no ground connection, so it cannot run and its peripherals and I2C/UART lines have no reference.

anomalies.observed: The LDO output net is +3.3V (REG3.1 OUT, sensors, decoupling). The MCU and pull-up rail is a separate net named +3V3, which has no regulator output on it. Only NAVC2.1 (VBAT) sits on +3V3. All MCU VDD pins (FCC2 pins 11, 27, 50, 75, 100; NAVC2 pins 19, 32, 48, 64) are unconnected.
anomalies.expected: The 3.3 V LDO output should feed the MCU VDD pins and the I2C pull-ups, so the MCUs are powered from the regulated rail.

evidence.quote: 3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs

anomalies.impact: If the rails are truly separate, the MCUs get no supply and the I2C pull-ups float on an unpowered rail. The board would not boot.

parsed.summary: The most concrete deviation is UART3_FCC2 pins 3 and 4 wired to the FCC2 VCAP regulator-output pins, which is an illogical bridge between a connector and a power_out pin. Ground and supply connections to the navigation MCU are also missing or unclear, which may be a further fault, so confidence is moderate.
